solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wicked stunner with wicked heart

indicators.note: the second wicked is placed at the heart of the word for a stunner, splitting it open

parts.note: a stunner, a gorgeous person, is a dish in slang
wicked means evil

explanation.surface: A beautiful person who is rotten to the core.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator is 'with ... heart'. 'Wicked' appears twice: once as the definition, once as the piece set in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something devilish is fiendishly cruel, a straightforward synonym for wicked.

clue.text: A duck found on English river

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so nil

explanation.surface: A duck is spotted floating on a river in England.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a batsman's score of zero in cricket; the surface wants a bird on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great river of Egypt, an example of a river.

clue.text: Handles leader of socialist party turning up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read from the bottom upward, so backwards
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a revel is a lively party

explanation.surface: The head of a left-wing party arrives at the meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses S plus REVEL, giving the whole run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Levers are bars or knobs you grip to operate a machine, i.e. handles.

clue.text: Police chief contains damage, feeling hurt

indicators.note: contains signals that the singer's name holds the second piece inside it

parts.note: Sting was the frontman, the chief, of the rock band the Police
to mar is to damage or spoil

explanation.surface: A senior police officer limits the damage while nursing wounded pride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Police' looks like the constabulary, but it is the band, whose lead singer was Sting.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarting describes the stinging pain of an injury or insult, so feeling hurt.

clue.text: Ben-Hur, perhaps, where a dust-up is held in acclaim

indicators.note: is held in says the first pieces sit inside the word for acclaim

parts.note: to cheer is to acclaim
a dust-up is a brawl or riot

explanation.surface: A scuffle breaks out among cheering crowds at a famous Hollywood epic.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben-Hur, in the novel and film, drives a chariot in the famous race, so he is an example of a charioteer.

clue.text: Terribly slim, consuming ends of uneatable cereal

indicators.note: consuming means the word slim takes the end letters inside it
terribly suggests the letters of slim are badly jumbled
the ends of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone frightfully thin eats only the inedible scraps of their breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends of' takes U and E from uneatable; 'consuming' puts them in SLIM and 'Terribly' shuffles the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Muesli is a Swiss-style breakfast mix of oats, nuts and fruit, a kind of cereal.

clue.text: Prince possibly taking on core of 'Time' band

indicators.note: taking on means the royal stand-in takes in the middle letters

parts.note: a prince may rule as regent for an underage monarch, as the Prince Regent did

indicators.note: the core of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: A royal joins a rock band called Time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'core of' and 'taking on' are the indicators. The quotation marks round 'Time' make it look like the band's name, when band is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment is a body of soldiers, and band can mean a group of people, as in a band of soldiers.

clue.text: Recite the rhyme holding rope

indicators.note: holding says the phrase contains the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: A child chants a nursery verse while gripping a skipping rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' points to the run spanning reciTE THE Rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: A tether is a rope or chain tying an animal to a post.

clue.text: Man controlling jumbo?

parts.note: jumbo suggests a jumbo jet and a pilot, but here it means an elephant and the person who drives it

explanation.walkthrough: Jumbo is a nickname for an elephant, after a famous Victorian zoo elephant; the surface suggests a jet pilot.
explanation.definitionFit: A mahout is the keeper and driver of a working elephant in South Asia.

clue.text: Tart possessing large mansion

indicators.note: possessing means the pastry word has the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: a tart is a kind of pie
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A loose woman owns an enormous country house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' leans toward the insulting sense; it is the pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile is informal for a large imposing house, such as a stately home.

clue.text: Go in force for campaign

parts.note: to go in is to enter
to prise is to force open with a lever

explanation.surface: Troops advance in strength as part of a military operation.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprise is a bold undertaking or project, much like a campaign.

clue.text: Failure hitched to useless other half

parts.note: a miss is a failure to hit
US is an abbreviation for unserviceable, i.e. useless

explanation.surface: A loser is married to a good-for-nothing partner.
explanation.walkthrough: US for useless (unserviceable) is a crossword convention; 'hitched to' is a joke about marriage as well as the join.
explanation.definitionFit: Missus is informal British slang for a wife, whom a husband may call his other half.

clue.text: Skill displayed in the main by 26?

definitions.text: Skill displayed in the main by 26?

parts.words: Skill displayed in the main by 26?
parts.note: the main is the open sea, as in the Spanish Main, and 26 across is a sailor, so this is a mariner's craft

explanation.walkthrough: The main is an old word for the high sea; 'in the main' pretends to mean mostly.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill in handling a ship at sea is precisely the meaning of the word.

clue.text: Police comeback after record is nothing irregular

indicators.note: after places the police piece behind the other pieces

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: comeback means the police initials are read in reverse

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: A police force's revival after a record of failure proves patchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeback' and 'after' are the indicators. CID, the British plain-clothes detective branch, is a common crossword shorthand for police.
explanation.definitionFit: Episodic means happening in occasional separate bursts, so irregular.

clue.text: Steed around start of Avengers getting rough

indicators.note: around means the horse word wraps itself round the single letter

parts.note: a steed is a horse

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: John Steed from The Avengers is having a tough time.
explanation.walkthrough: John Steed was the hero of the 1960s British TV series The Avengers, which the surface evokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarse voice is harsh and croaky, which is to say rough.

clue.text: Queen following ought to support 'Under Pressure'

indicators.note: following puts the royal abbreviation after the modal verb

parts.note: ought to means should
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A fan says the band Queen should back their hit Under Pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen and Under Pressure point to the rock band and their song; Queen is ER, and to shoulder is to bear a burden under strain.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoulder a load is to bear its weight, supporting it under strain.

clue.text: Feels sorry for topless birds

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed

parts.note: to regret something is to feel sorry for it

explanation.surface: Someone pities half-naked young women, with birds as British slang for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' drops R from the start of REGRETS; birds is British slang for young women, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Egrets are white wading herons, examples of birds.

clue.text: Model minces about holding case of perfume

indicators.note: holding means the shuffled letters keep the outside letters inside them
about signals the letters of minces are moved around
the case of a word is its outer letters

explanation.surface: A catwalk model sashays around carrying a bottle of scent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges MINCES into SCIMEN; 'case of' gives P and E from perfume, which 'holding' places inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is a sample or example, so a model of its kind.

clue.text: Glib one's grasping old lingo

parts.note: pat means glib, too slick
one is I, and one's gives I plus S

explanation.surface: A smooth talker clings to old-fashioned language.
explanation.definitionFit: A patois is a local dialect, an informal tongue or lingo.

clue.text: Described by a throw before a strike back?

definitions.text: Described by a throw before a strike back?

indicators.note: back signals the whole sequence is read in reverse
before puts the throw ahead of the second part

parts.note: to lob is to throw high
a rap is a sharp strike

explanation.surface: A bowler sends down a delivery ahead of a retaliatory blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns A LOB A RAP into the answer. The whole clue also defines: a thrown object traces this curve.
explanation.definitionFit: The path of a projectile under gravity is this curve, so it is what a throw traces out.

clue.text: Airhead blonde's on fire

parts.note: the head of air is its first letter
light means pale or fair, as blonde hair is

explanation.surface: A dim blonde is burning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Airhead' looks like an insult for the blonde; split it as air plus head, its first letter. The 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Alight means burning or lit, so on fire.

clue.text: Direction past British frontier

indicators.note: past means the direction word comes after the abbreviation

parts.note: an order is a direction or command

explanation.surface: Orders arrive beyond the British border post.
explanation.definitionFit: A border is the line where one country meets another, a frontier.

clue.text: Elitist returned with excellent Oriental art

indicators.note: returned means the word for an elitist is read backwards

parts.note: a snob is an elitist
A1 means excellent, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A snob comes home with superb Far Eastern artworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses SNOB to BONS; A1, first-rate, supplies AI.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonsai is the Japanese art of growing miniature trees in pots.

clue.text: New lot isn't prepared for Hollywood

indicators.note: prepared signals the letters are made up into something new

explanation.surface: A film studio's new backlot is not ready for the shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges NEW, LOT and ISNT; lot also hints at a studio backlot.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinseltown is a nickname for Hollywood, playing on its glitter and superficiality.

clue.text: Turned on following Sun's opening

indicators.note: following puts the lit word after the abbreviation for Sun

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for Sunday or sun; the 's adds no letter
lit means turned on, as a lamp is

explanation.surface: A lamp is switched on as the sun starts to rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' reads as the start of the day but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A slit is a narrow cut or opening.

clue.text: Some con artists may, initially

indicators.note: initially means only the first letters of the four words are taken

explanation.surface: Some swindlers may try something, at first.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters give the answer, and the whole clue describes what con artists may pull.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a swindle, the trick that con artists practise.

clue.text: Quiet religious leader in Eastern temple

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A silent holy man sits in a temple in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrine is a holy place of worship, much like a temple.

clue.text: Sailor and prophet to traverse afar

indicators.note: to traverse means the prophet word spans across the other letters

parts.note: a seer is a prophet

explanation.surface: A mariner and a soothsayer set out to cross distant lands.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafarer is someone who travels by sea, a sailor.
